message:
Rob, I think there's more than material wealth driving the circumstance of PBR's hipness, as perhaps (incompletely) evidenced by [this Washington Post story](http://sixmile.clemson.edu/pbr.htm) from a couple years ago, or [this brief observation](http://www.frogdesign.com/mind/) (ninth paragraph down) on "brand irony." So yeah, I think you might have a market for that Hudey after all, pardner -- but really, what you're saying about wealth being a factor in addition to ironic hipness totally reinforces my overall point anyway, which is that class and cultural valuation are overdetermined; shaped and influences by far too many factors for us to be able to point to any single one as determinate.

Jim, I might argue that the "brand maturity" was reached a generation ago (my Uncle Stanley has some old PBR-branded bar coasters and a PBR neon sign in his kitchen), which is what allowed for the ironic twist from today's generation. Can I ask which Foucault essays you're thinking of?
